[MUQATIL:17:19-21/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The righteous who seek the Hereafter do its proper work while affirming God's oneness; God thanks their effort by rewarding them with Paradise.
[MUQATIL:17:19-21/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | reports | The verse was revealed concerning Bilal the muezzin and others.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r5] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | Striving for the Hereafter means doing the deeds appropriate to it, with sincere faith.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r6] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan reports the Prophet saying God does not accept a servant’s deed until He is pleased with the servant’s utterance.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r7] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The promised accepted striving means the person’s deeds, which God thanks and rewards with Paradise.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r8] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī says the thankful reward means God repays them for their deeds.
[IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p274#2/r6] IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL, d. 276 · author | holds | Saʿy can mean work or action: seeking the afterlife with its saʿy means doing the work it requires.
[TAB-FULL:v14p537/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The afterlife-seeker works the work appropriate to it: obedience that pleases God, while believing in God's reward, unlike the worldly seeker who denies it.
[TAB-FULL:v14p537/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | In سعى لها سعيها, the feminine pronoun refers to the afterlife; the wording means doing the work of the afterlife.
[TAB-FULL:v14p537/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | God thanks these believers by rewarding their good works well and forgiving their bad ones through mercy.
[TAB-FULL:v14p537/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda says God rewards their good deeds and overlooks their bad deeds.
[SULAMI:v1p385/r1] SULAMI, d. 412 · القاسم | reports | Al-Qasim says seeking the afterlife requires rightly directed effort: it must accord with the law and be grounded in faith, since outwardly upright seekers may lack lasting faith and good efforts may go unaccepted.
[SULAMI:v1p385/r2] SULAMI, d. 412 · بعضهم | reports | Some distinguish bodily striving in worldly life, striving with hearts toward the afterlife, and striving toward God through spiritual aspiration.
[SULAMI:v1p385/r3] SULAMI, d. 412 · أبو حفص | reports | Abu Hafs says praised striving is free from ostentation, reputation-seeking, self-regard, and desire for reward, being purely for God alone.
[THALABI:v6p91/r8] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The afterlife seeker must strive properly and be a believer; such striving is accepted rather than rejected.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās understands the Hereafter as Paradise; the commentators also relate the phrase to seeking the reward or good of the Hereafter, as in 3:145. | mentions 3:145
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Striving for the Hereafter means carrying out God's obligations and fulfilling His rights.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p293/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The striving is accepted only with faith, since God accepts no good deed except from a believer; gratitude means multiplying good deeds, erasing sins, and raising ranks.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r3] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Seeking the afterlife means seeking Paradise and fulfilling God's obligations; faith is necessary because God accepts good only from believers.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r4] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The believers' accepted efforts are appreciated by multiplying their good deeds.
[DAMGHANI:v1p237/r1] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Saʿy means work or action; the examples describe a person’s effort and work being accepted. | mentions 92:4, 22:51, 34:5
[JISHUMI:v6p4183/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | reports | The passage urges seeking the afterlife: its seeker attains it and may also attain worldly good, whereas a worldly seeker may attain neither.
[JISHUMI:v6p4183/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The praiseworthy effort that merits Paradise requires faith and good works, against the Murjiʾa.
[JISHUMI:v6p4183/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The disobedience and willing mentioned are human acts, supporting the author's doctrine of created acts.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r7] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Afterlife-seekers must strive as its pursuit requires and be believers; their effort is accepted.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r10] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The praised effort is the proper effort and its due allotment of righteous deeds.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r11] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | Three conditions make effort rewarded: seeking the afterlife and turning away from delusion, performing commanded acts and avoiding prohibitions, and sound faith.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r12] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · بعض المتقدمين | reports | An early authority says works do not benefit without three things: firm faith, sincere intention, and correct action, and cites this verse.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r13] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | God's gratitude means His reward for obedience.
[KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r3] KASHSHAF-FULL, d. 538 · author | holds | The pious believer has chosen the afterlife's riches and is indifferent to worldly allotment; worldly poverty may even help the goal.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Seeking the afterlife requires certain belief in it, in God, and in His messages; these elements are interdependent.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The required effort is sustained good works and speech according to the law; God rewards and forgives deeds He thanks.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · النبي | reports | A report says God thanked and forgave a man who gave water to a thirsty dog.
[TABRISI:17:19-22/r2] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Seeking the hereafter requires obedience, avoiding sins, and belief in God's unity and messengers; the effort is accepted.
[TABRISI:17:19-22/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · قتادة | reports | He says God's gratitude consists in multiplying good deeds and overlooking sins.
[TABRISI:17:19-22/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · الحسن | reports | He urges pursuit of the hereafter: its seeker attains it and may also gain the world, while a worldly seeker may fail at both.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p349/r6] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · المفسرون | reports | The third sense is deeds or striving: the source applies it both to striving for the afterlife and to people's divergent efforts.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#3/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Seeking the afterlife means seeking Paradise and performing the deeds appropriate to it; faith is required for deeds to be valid, and God accepts, rewards, and praises this striving.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The names of the vowel marks derive from articulation: ḍamma closes and raises the lips, fatḥa opens the mouth, and kasra lowers the jaw; jazm means cutting, while the senses of waqf and sukūn are evident.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · بعضهم | reports | Some grammarians reserve fatḥa, ḍamma, kasra, and waqf for built forms, while the other four terms name inflectional states.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · آخرون | reports | Others use the first four names for both built and inflected states, treating the second four as narrower names for inflection; the first set is thus genus to the second.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · سيبويه | reports | Sībawayh calls the vocalic states al-majārī and counts eight.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Al-Rāzī explains the name al-majārī by saying the so-called movement is a voiced sound produced as breath flows and extends after a consonant.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · المازني | reports | Al-Māzinī says Sībawayh errs by calling the states of built words al-majārī, since only changing inflectional states should count as things that flow.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p48#2/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | rejects | Al-Rāzī replies that built forms change between connected speech and pause, so their states are not wholly fixed and can still be called al-majārī.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The first condition is intending the afterlife’s reward; without that intention an act does not benefit, as the verse about human striving and the saying about intentions indicate. | mentions 53:39
[RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Intention matters because the purpose of deeds is to illuminate the heart through knowing and loving God, which requires intending worship and obedience.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The second condition is pursuing the afterlife by valid acts of worship; idolatrous approaches remain invalid even when their practitioners intend devotion.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Some idolaters claim they cannot worship God directly, so they worship stars or angels as devoted intermediaries; Razi rejects this as invalid.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Others say their idols depict prophets and saints and are meant to secure their intercession; Razi also rejects this path.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p143/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | He also reports that people in India seek closeness to God by killing or burning themselves, but says this too is an invalid route.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | When afterlife motive outweighs worldly motive, Razi presents disagreement: a divine report rejects works involving association, while one analysis denies purity if motives combine and another accepts the dominant afterlife motive.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Equal motives or a

stronger worldly motive are agreed to make the act unaccepted, though either is better than seeking worldly benefit alone.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | On acting without any motive, those who require a motive say it cannot occur; those who do not require one deem it inwardly ineffective and outwardly forbidden as pointless.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Faith is the third condition; without it acts of piety do not earn reward, while meeting all three conditions makes the effort appreciated and accepted.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Gratitude comprises recognizing the recipient as a benefactor, praising them verbally, and acting in ways that honor them; God treats the obedient in all three ways.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · جعفر بن حرب | reports | Jaʿfar ibn Harb argues that faith must be created by God because otherwise thanking God for it would be improper praise for another’s act. | mentions 3:188
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ثمامة بن الأشرس | reports | Thumama replies that people thank God for the capacity, intellect, revealed books, and proofs He provides, while God thanks them for the faith they perform.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Razi reconciles the positions: God supplies the complete power and motive, while the servant performs the act of faith, so both God and servant can rightly receive thanks.
[RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | He classifies actions by whether they aim at worldly good, afterlife good, both together, or neither; the verse directly treats the first two.
[QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r3] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Seeking the afterlife means doing its deeds of obedience while believing, since acts are accepted only from a believer; the effort is accepted, not rejected.
[QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r4] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Another explanation of gratitude is that good deeds are multiplied tenfold, seventyfold, seven hundredfold, or many times over.
[QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r5] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو هريرة | reports | When asked about a millionfold reward for a good deed, Abu Hurayra says he heard the Prophet promise two millionfold.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The proper effort for the afterlife means doing what is commanded and avoiding what is forbidden, rather than inventing acts of devotion.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The preposition in “strives for it” signals intention and sincerity.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Faith must be sound, without either associating partners with God or denial; it is the essential condition.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:17:19-20/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Those who meet the three conditions have effort accepted by God and recompensed; God’s thanking obedience means rewarding it.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | The phrase about striving for the afterlife can mean making it the direct object of striving, or performing the effort it deserves through adequate righteous deeds.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Faith means affirming God's promises and threats.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | A believer's afterlife-directed effort is accepted by God and rewarded.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p282#2/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · بعض السلف | reports | Some early authorities say deeds do not benefit without three conditions: firm faith, sincere intention, and sound action; the verse requires afterlife intent, commanded effort, and firm faith.
[QASHANI:17:18-21/r3] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | The hereafter-seeker has pure readiness and a sound original nature; when faith and good works fulfill its true conditions, God rewards the effort by granting its object.
[QASHANI:17:18-21/r4] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | True desire and seeking arise only with readiness; the desired perfection already exists potentially in the decree, and proper effort brings it from unseen potential into visible actuality.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Seeking the afterlife means preferring it, intending it, and pursuing the deeds prescribed for salvation; faith is the indispensable condition without which intention and effort do not save.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · بعض المتقدمين | reports | An early authority says work is useless without firm faith, sincere intention, and sound action, and cites this verse.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The plural أولئك refers to people described by the singular relative من because its meaning is collective; God rewards and praises their obedience, while He alone truly deserves gratitude.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | God’s thanking a servant means praising and rewarding the obedient person; the human response is praise for reason, revelation, books, and proofs granted by God.
[SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | سعيها has two parses: direct object meaning the deeds appropriate to the Hereafter, or a cognate accusative with لها meaning for its sake.
[SAMIN-DURR:17:19/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | وهو مؤمن is a circumstantial clause describing the subject of سعى.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Seeking the afterlife means seeking its abode and delights by the proper path, namely following the Messenger.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p63/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The seeker must believe in the heart, affirming reward and requital; then the person’s effort is accepted and appreciated.
[BURHAN:v2p129/r3] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The hadith that actions depend on intentions has an explicit Quranic basis in the contrast between seeking the immediate world and the Hereafter, and in accountability for what hearts intend and oaths they bind.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Whether worldly provision is present or absent, it neither honors nor disgraces its recipient; real status before God comes from deeds.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Seeking the afterlife must be joined to its proper effort: actions pleasing to God as prescribed in the Book and Sunna, not unsupported practices; intention needs action, actually when possible and by capacity when not.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · بعض السلف | reports | Some early authorities say work is useless without established faith, sincere intention, and correct action; the author identifies this firmness with the surah's ideal of excellence.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The afterlife seeker must be a steadfast believer; only then is the effort accepted and repaid with multiplied reward.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Worldly wealth may be given to David and Solomon for God's favored work or withheld from another as an honor, never as humiliation; status before God depends on deeds.
[DURR-FULL:v5p254/r10] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · قتادة | reports | God thanks the person for a little good and overlooks much of the person's shortcomings.
[BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Seeking the afterlife requires its fitting effort: obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions, not invented devotional practices; the lām marks intention and sincerity.
[BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The seeker must also have sound faith without association or denial; these three conditions yield effort accepted by God and rewarded, with gratitude meaning reward for obedience.
[BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Human beings combine worldly and otherworldly elements: the lower self tends toward Hell, the spirit toward Paradise, and the heart can turn toward either divine wrath or grace.
[BURSEVI:v5p110#2/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | By divine wrath a heart turns toward worldly desire and separation; by grace it turns upward, seeks the afterlife sincerely, and trusts that whoever seeks God finds Him, so its effort is appreciated by the eternal Originator.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Seeking the afterlife means seeking its lasting abode and blessings, while its proper effort is fulfilling commands and avoiding prohibitions.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Some construe the effort as an act done for the afterlife or as effort suited to it; either way, invented worship by unbelievers does not qualify.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The lām signals purpose or special relation and thus requires intention and sincerity toward God in the deed.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | Some say there is no need to understand the earlier desire as desire through deeds, since the following phrase already describes the effort; on this reading the same need not be supplied for the prior verse. | mentions 17:18
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The person must have sound faith, and the circumstantial clause shows faith must accompany both desire and effort; without it neither suffices.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعض المتقدمين | reports | A saying from an early authority says useful work requires firm faith, sincere intention, and sound action, and cites this verse.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Those points to the people just described; the plural both respects the meaning of من and hints that their reward arrives together, while their elevated status is signaled by distance.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author

 | holds | Their effort is accepted and rewarded; commentators differ on whether سعي refers to all the prior qualifying deeds or only the effort just named, whose centrality the wording highlights.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p47#2/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The root sense of سعي is brisk walking, below running, and it often denotes striving in good deeds; Alusi cites alqama ibn Sad's verse as evidence.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The afterlife seeker represents a clear spiritual disposition and sound nature, and makes the effort suited to it by following the path approved by revealed law. | mentions 17:19
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | Some distinguish bodily striving for worldly aims, striving with the heart for the afterlife, and striving with focused aspiration for God.
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | True faith remains firm and is not shaken by storms of doubt; the accepted effort is rewarded. | mentions 17:19
[ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أبو حفص | reports | Abu Hafs defines appreciated effort as free of ostentation, reputation-seeking, self-regard, and desire for compensation, dedicated solely to God.
[ELMALILI:17:19-22/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The afterlife-seeker must pursue it with fitting effort while believing; such people’s striving is appreciated.
[ELMALILI:17:19-22/r6] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Every effort needs power; the greatest power is truth and truth begins with monotheism, making faith the first condition for afterlife-worthy striving and explaining why the commands begin with tawhid.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The surrounding passage gradually teaches that people acquire their own deeds by choice and bear their own account. | mentions 17:13, 17:15
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The afterlife-minded group knows true success lies beyond this life, follows divinely guided works through the messengers, and is rewarded according to its aspiration.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The contrast between the two sentences supplies an added, contextual restriction: the first person wants the immediate world alone.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The present tense depicts renewed worldly desire, while the past tense and omitted kāna make afterlife desire sound settled and especially worthy.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Saʿy literally means walking rather than running; here it denotes good works that lead to the afterlife as a traveler reaches a destination.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The possessive construction is a verbal noun related semantically to its object, and saʿy is an absolute object specifying kind.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Wanting the afterlife without striving is self-deception; any aim needs the actions that bring it about.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · عبد الله بن المبارك | reports | Ibn al-Mubārak’s poem rebukes hoping for salvation without following its path, like expecting a ship to sail on dry land.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The circumstantial clause is nominal to signal stable, enduring faith; Ibn ʿĀshūr compares this to the wording about persevering believers. | mentions 90:17
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The demonstrative points out that people described as seeking the afterlife merit the announced reward.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Calling the effort thanked is a rational metaphor: the worker is approved, and describing the work conveys approval of its doer.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p61/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Kāna indicates that the effort was already worthy of thanks in worldly life, while obedience also brings later reward.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | After discussing worldly destruction following a prophetic mission, the passage turns to afterlife punishment, reward, and the general principle governing both.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · الراغب | reports | Saʿy means brisk walking, less than running, and is also used for earnest effort toward good or evil.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The afterlife sought here means the next life itself, and the earlier argument also rejects narrowing the phrase to intending it through one's deeds.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The possessive wording makes the effort specific to the afterlife: one must strive in a manner fitting for it, exerting full effort in good deeds grounded in certain reason or legal proof.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r6] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Belief means God and entails divine oneness, prophethood, and resurrection; the explicit condition requires sound belief including tawhid and acknowledgment of prophethood.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | God thanks the believers' effort by accepting it well and praising its doer; both reward and subsequent praise are grace, with praise being grace upon grace.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#17/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Afterlife-directed deeds reliably reach their ends, unlike worldly causes, since God says the effort is thanked but worldly provision is only what He wills for whom He wills.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · روح المعاني | reports | A reported taxonomy divides agents into those seeking this world, the afterlife, both, or neither; mixed motives then divide according to which desire predominates or whether they are equal.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r8] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · روح المعاني | reports | The reported discussion says scholars disagree over accepting mixed-motive deeds when afterlife intent predominates, but agree against deeds where worldly motive predominates or ties.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · روح المعاني | reports | The fourth type is impossible for those who require every voluntary act to have a motive; others say such an act has no inner effect but remains outwardly forbidden.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | rejects | These verses classify a person's ultimate life-goal, not the acceptance of every individual act: seeking this world treats it as the end, while seeking the afterlife treats this world as a stage toward it.
[TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Afterlife-seekers can still fail to strive properly or lack belief, but the verse selects the believing person whose effort fits the afterlife because it identifies the roots of happiness and misery.
[ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | Here 'believer' entails recognizing God's absolute oneness and willingly accepting guidance through prophetic revelation, since striving for the hereafter presupposes belief and accountability.
[ASAD-NOTES:17:19#n24/r2] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | Although the Arabic sentence is singular before the final clause, Asad renders the pronouns in the plural to match that clause and normal Arabic usage.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-surah-maryam-19:p381/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Section III invites Jews and Quraysh to the Qur’an's natural straight path, contrasts the fates of acceptance and rejection, rebukes those blind to signs who demand punishment, and alludes to God's practice of punishing nations.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-surah-maryam-19:p386/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Those who seek the Hereafter and make the fitting effort succeed there while receiving whatever worldly share God ordained for them.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-surah-maryam-19:p386/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Desire for the Hereafter alone is insufficient: it must be joined to fitting effort and faith free of polytheism.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | Worldly advantages are not true superiority; seeking the hereafter concerns one's aim, not merely the type of work, since worldly tasks can serve the hereafter and worship can serve worldly gain.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r3] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Hz. Peygamber | reports | The Prophet teaches that deeds are judged according to intentions.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r4] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | A person seeks the hereafter by doing even worldly work honestly under God's rules, remembering accountability, and hoping for God's reward; each receives according to intention.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r5] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Zemahşerî | reports | A good deed requires seeking afterlife reward, performing the actions that earn it, and doing so with faith; faith makes the other conditions meaningful and effective.
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p592/r2] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | In conditional clauses, he uses the present for actions expected to recur and the past for actions that do not or should not recur; examples include repeated gratitude versus one-time disbelief and accidental versus deliberate killing. | mentions 17:18, 17:19, 31:12, 4:92, 4:93
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p95/r2] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | The past marks desire for the one afterlife as a single act; present tense marks recurrent desires for reward, which arise with each deed. | mentions 17:19, 3:145
[STUDYQURAN:17:18/r2] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | God appreciates sincere believers’ efforts for the Hereafter; His appreciation, literally thankfulness, is their reward there. | mentions 2:200, 2:201, 3:145
